lesson.subtitle: Lesson 8 -- Christmas at Rockefeller Center
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Carlos Henrique Rodrigues | Lesson 8 -- Christmas at Rockefeller Center
lesson.grammar_point: past simple of be (was, were, was not, Was it...?)

listenings.text: When I was nineteen, my family and I were in New York for Christmas. It was very cold, and there was snow on the streets. The Christmas tree at Rockefeller Center was huge. My dad was very excited about the ice rink. But on the ice, he was very nervous! I was next to him all the time. Was it a perfect day? No, it wasn't. But we were so happy.

I was at the Rockefeller Center rink for forty years. I was the person with the skates. Every December, the crowd was big, and the visitors were from everywhere: Brazil, Japan, Italy. My favorite visitors? The fathers. They were always sure: "I was a great skater when I was young!" Then they were on the ice, and their children were the teachers. It was always funny.

extra_audio.text: Carlos was in New York with his family at Christmas. There was a big Christmas tree at Rockefeller Center. Carlos was the teacher, and all the theory was perfect. Then the skates were on his feet. On the ice, his legs were not strong. His daughter was the teacher, and it was very funny.

paras: Some years ago, Carlos was in New York with his family at Christmas. His daughter was twenty-one. The city was very cold, and the streets were full of people. Some things were not like the movies, but Rockefeller Center was beautiful.

There was a giant Christmas tree, and there was an ice rink under the tree. The crowd was big. When Carlos was young, skating was very popular in Brazil, and he was a good skater. So he was the teacher: "To stop, you cross your legs. To turn, you do this." All the theory was perfect.

Then the skates were on his feet, and he was on the ice. Surprise: his legs were not strong, and he was not able to stand up! Five minutes later, his daughter was the teacher, and Carlos was the student. Was it a bad day? No, it was a very funny day. Theory and practice were two different things.
